name: lr_help
title: How LrC-AVG works
description: Explain how LrC-AVG works: sessions and session_id, what uses a pass, previews and region previews, the metrics, Variants mode, clipping guardrails, mask names, logs and errors. Static text; touches nothing.

name: lr_get_active_photo_context
title: Active photo context
description: Describe the photo selected in Lightroom Classic: file, GPS position (`gps`, null for none), EXIF (ISO, shutter in seconds, aperture, focal length, lens, camera), rating/label/pick, process version, camera profile, and every Develop setting under its canonical name (`settings`; these names are the ones lr_step takes). `pipeline` is "raw" (camera raw files) or "rendered" (JPEG, TIFF, PNG, PSD, HEIC, AVIF and other non-raw files): `white_balance_unit` says what temperature and tint mean on this photo, Kelvin on raw, a relative -100..100 on rendered. Rendered photos have their own profiles (Color, Monochrome). Also says whether a session is open on it, and which Lightroom version runs (`lightroom`; tell the user its `notices`, empty when the version is supported and tested). `left_open` lists sessions an engine that stopped (the AI client closed or restarted it) left open, with `left_open_note`: ask the user, for each, to revert, accept or abandon it, and end it with lr_end_session. Changes nothing.

name: lr_get_preview
title: Preview of the active photo
description: Render the photo selected in Lightroom with its current Develop settings (a JPEG export, quality 75, which takes about 3 seconds) and return it as an image, with its uuid, SHA-256 hash, size, metrics and timings. With `uuid`: that photo instead, without selecting it (to look through a shoot, for culling or keywording). With `session_id`: the session's photo (refused with TARGET_CHANGED if another photo is selected) and its region metrics; in Variants mode `target` names the copy, which is selected in Lightroom first. With `region` (a box in 0-1 of the preview you see (the photo as cropped in Lightroom, upright), from its top-left corner, as mask geometry and lr_set_regions are): a crop of that box for judging sharpness, noise or fringing; the photo is exported larger (up to 4096 px) so the crop fills `long_edge`, never enlarged; `effective_scale` = output pixels per photo pixel (1 = 100 %). With `region`, the result's `metrics` describe the whole export (`metrics_scope` "frame") and `crop_metrics` the requested box, both measured at export resolution. Changes nothing. Metrics are measured on the rendered preview (8-bit sRGB, as Lightroom exported it), not on the raw file: clipping here can often be recovered with highlights/whites or shadows/blacks. clip_high_pct = % of pixels with any channel >= 253; clip_high_tone_pct = % with 2+ channels >= 253 (the high guard's); clip_low_pct = % with all channels <= 2; luma = Rec. 709 on the 8-bit values; luma_percentiles p1-p99 by nearest rank; dynamic_range = (p99 - p1) / 255; rb_ratio = mean red / mean blue; saturation_mean = mean HSV saturation, 0-100; hue_histogram = 12 bins of 30 degrees (bin i centred on i*30: 0 red, 60 yellow, 120 green, 180 cyan, 240 blue, 300 magenta), % of the chromatic pixels (HSV saturation and value >= 0.1, chromatic_pct of all); hue_mean = their circular mean hue in degrees; sharpness = Laplacian variance of luma at 512 px (more = detail or noise). Percentages are 0-100.

session_id.description: render the session's photo, with its region metrics; refused if another photo is selected; ignored when no session is open

target.description: with session_id, in Variants mode: the photo, "A", "B", "C" or "master" (default: the photo the last session call worked on, the pick once there is one)

region.description: return a crop of this box {x, y, w, h} in 0-1 of the preview you see (the photo as cropped in Lightroom, upright), from its top-left corner, exported large enough to show it at up to 100 %; see effective_scale

uuid.description: render this photo (a uuid from lr_search_photos, lr_get_selected_photos or lr_import_photos), selected or not; the selection is not touched; not with session_id

quality.description: "exact" (default): the export, about 3 s. "fast": Lightroom's cached preview, quicker but possibly stale (source "thumbnail", stale_possible true); for browsing, not for judging an edit; not with session_id, target or region

Metrics are measured on the rendered preview (8-bit sRGB, as Lightroom exported it), not on the raw file: clipping here can often be recovered with highlights/whites or shadows/blacks. clip_high_pct = % of pixels with any channel >= 253; clip_high_tone_pct = % with 2+ channels >= 253 (the high guard's); clip_low_pct = % with all channels <= 2; luma = Rec. 709 on the 8-bit values; luma_percentiles p1-p99 by nearest rank; dynamic_range = (p99 - p1) / 255; rb_ratio = mean red / mean blue; saturation_mean = mean HSV saturation, 0-100; hue_histogram = 12 bins of 30 degrees (bin i centred on i*30: 0 red, 60 yellow, 120 green, 180 cyan, 240 blue, 300 magenta), % of the chromatic pixels (HSV saturation and value >= 0.1, chromatic_pct of all); hue_mean = their circular mean hue in degrees; sharpness = Laplacian variance of luma at 512 px (more = detail or noise). Percentages are 0-100.

name: lr_get_photo_stats
title: Metrics of several photos
description: Measure up to 20 photos named by uuid, without a session and without selecting them: each is exported at 800 px (about 1-3 s a photo) and measured. Returns `photos` in the order given, each with `metrics` (the summary lr_get_preview returns, sharpness included) or its own `error`. For culling: compare sharpness and exposure across frames of one scene. Returns no images. Not while a session is open. Changes nothing. A call works for about 30 seconds, then stops starting new photos and returns `not_yet` and `next`, saying how to go on: keep calling until `not_yet` is gone, and tell the user how far along it is. A call still busy at 50 seconds returns `pending` with `next`. Percentages are 0-100.

uuids.description: 1-20 photo uuids (from lr_search_photos or lr_get_selected_photos)

name: lr_begin_session
title: Begin an editing session
description: Start an editing session on the photo selected in Lightroom. THE USER'S REQUEST COMES FIRST: put it in `notes` in their own words. An intent (lr_list_intents) is an optional starting point: leave intent_id out when none fits; pass `profile` or `guardrails` when the request needs them (e.g. high key or crushed blacks). The engine makes a Develop snapshot "AVG pre-session …" (lr_end_session revert returns to it), renders the photo, and runs pass 0 as one History step "AVG <id> pass 0/N". Returns session_id, the intent's brief, guardrails, pass0_applied, the full settings, metrics, the preview, `log_path`, and `start_off_zero` (settings found on the photo, which may be import defaults or earlier edits). Then call lr_step once per pass, up to max_passes. One session at a time; it stays open until lr_end_session. A photo with a session an engine that stopped left open (lr_get_active_photo_context `left_open`) is refused with SESSION_LEFT_OPEN, nothing written, until that session is ended. lr_help explains passes, variants mode, clipping guardrails, metrics and previews. The LrC-AVG HUD in Lightroom opens and follows the session; there the user can Abort (the photo goes back to the pre-session snapshot, and a running call stops before its next write), Accept (after the running call), Pick a copy, or Approve a pass (approve_each_pass mode). A session the user ended answers every later call with SESSION_ENDED (details: outcome, source); tell the user, and start a new session only if they ask.

intent_id.description: an intent id from lr_list_intents, e.g. landscape_golden_hour, as a starting point; leave out (or give "none") when no intent fits the user's request

profile.description: the profile pass 0 sets, replacing the intent's: a profile of the photo's pipeline (raw: e.g. "Adobe Color"; rendered: "Color" or "Monochrome")

clip_baseline.description: true only when the user's request asks pass 0 to pull clipping in; replaces the intent's

mode.description: "converge" (default): edit the selected photo; "variants": make virtual copies A, B (and C) with the intent's variant looks, then the user picks one

variant_count.description: mode "variants" only (ignored in Converge mode): how many copies, 2-3 (default: the settings page's, else 3); A, B, C take the intent's variants of those letters

max_passes.description: passes after pass 0, 1-16 (default: the settings page's, else 8)

guardrails.description: clipping limits for this session, replacing the intent's, the settings page's and the defaults (0.5 % high, 1.0 % low)

notes.description: the user's request in their own words, kept in the log; suggested on every session; it takes precedence over the intent's brief

model.description: Your own model name or id, shown to the user and logged; never used for decisions.

long_edge.description: Preview long edge in pixels, 800-1920, for the whole session (default: the settings page's, else 1600).

return_image.description: "after" (default): the new preview; "before_after": the previous and the new preview in one labelled image; "none": no image

name: lr_step
title: One editing pass
description: Apply one pass to the session's photo. `settings` maps canonical names to a CHANGE for numeric sliders (e.g. {"exposure": 0.3, "highlights": -20} adds 0.3 EV and lowers highlights by 20) and to the value to set for camera_profile, switches, booleans and curves. Each change is capped at the slider's per-pass maximum × the pass's decay (by default 1.0, 0.6, 0.4, 0.25 for passes 1-4, and a later pass takes the last value again; begin's session_settings.decay has the session's. Per-pass maxima: exposure 1 EV, contrast/texture/clarity/dehaze 40, highlights/shadows/whites/blacks 60, vibrance/saturation 30, temperature 1500 K on raw photos and 30 on rendered ones, whose temperature is relative, tint 30, HSL 40, grading 30; a grading hue is an angle: it takes the shorter way round, wraps at 360 and is not capped) and at the slider's range (`clamped`). The clipping guard covers only an end within its limit before the pass (every end when the session's `clip_baseline` is on; an end already over is left alone and reported `unmet`). A change that would push further into a guarded limit already reached is refused (`refused`); the rest is written as one History step "AVG <id> pass n/N", read back, rendered and measured. If clipping then exceeds a guarded limit, the engine pulls back the sliders that caused it, else takes fixed steps, at most 3 ("… guard k", in `guardrail_actions`). The pass is undone ("… clip revert" / "… region revert", a `reverted` action and `undone` in the result; the pass still counts) when clipping is still over a limit the photo was within before the pass, or a preserved region drifts; `applied` then lists what was written before the undo. Returns the applied changes, full settings, metrics, delta_metrics against the previous pass, and the image. `converged_by_metrics` (the metrics stopped moving) or `cap_reached` end the passes: then call lr_end_session. Unknown names or wrong types are refused before anything is written. Errors are {code, message, recoverable}: `recoverable`: true means the same call may work later unchanged (e.g. once Lightroom is back); false means change the call first. Variants mode: name the copy with `target`; each copy takes ONE pass before the pick (a second is refused with AWAITING_PICK), and the step that gives the last copy its pass returns `awaiting_pick: true` and the contact sheet: then ask the user to pick (lr_select_variant). After the pick, steps go to the pick, whose pass count carries on. `hud_actions` lists what the user did in the HUD since your last call (a pick), and a `deck_fallback` note when the Deck did not start and the classic HUD window opened instead (tell the user). approve_each_pass mode (begin's session_settings.approval): pass 1 needs no approval; from pass 2 on, the call first waits up to 40 s for the user's Approve of the pass before (the HUD's button, or lr_approve_pass after the user approved in chat), else returns AWAITING_APPROVAL (recoverable; nothing written, the pass not used): tell the user the pass waits for their Approve, then call again. Unknown names are refused before the wait. `approval` in the result says which pass was approved, by whom, and how long the call waited. Metrics are measured on the rendered preview (8-bit sRGB, as Lightroom exported it), not on the raw file: clipping here can often be recovered with highlights/whites or shadows/blacks. clip_high_pct = % of pixels with any channel >= 253; clip_high_tone_pct = % with 2+ channels >= 253 (the high guard's); clip_low_pct = % with all channels <= 2; luma = Rec. 709 on the 8-bit values; luma_percentiles p1-p99 by nearest rank; dynamic_range = (p99 - p1) / 255; rb_ratio = mean red / mean blue; saturation_mean = mean HSV saturation, 0-100; hue_histogram = 12 bins of 30 degrees (bin i centred on i*30: 0 red, 60 yellow, 120 green, 180 cyan, 240 blue, 300 magenta), % of the chromatic pixels (HSV saturation and value >= 0.1, chromatic_pct of all); hue_mean = their circular mean hue in degrees; sharpness = Laplacian variance of luma at 512 px (more = detail or noise). Percentages are 0-100.

target.description: Variants mode: the copy, "A", "B" or "C" (after lr_select_variant, the pick; it may be left out). Converge mode: "master" or left out

settings.description: canonical name -> CHANGE for numeric sliders (e.g. {"exposure": 0.3, "highlights": -20}); the value to set for camera_profile, switches, booleans and curves

rationale.description: one line: what you saw and why this change

return_image.description: "after" (default): the new preview; "before_after": the previous and the new preview in one labelled image; "none": no image

name: lr_probe
title: Probe slider sensitivity
description: Measure how 1-3 numeric sliders move the metrics on this photo: each is changed by `magnitude` × its per-pass maximum, rendered and measured (about 3.5 s each), and the photo is put back (History: "AVG <id> probe <slider>" … "probe revert"). Returns the metric change per unit of each slider; later lr_step calls use it to cap changes that would cross a clipping limit. Does not use a pass. Only when the intent sets allow_probe.

target.description: Variants mode: the copy to probe, as for lr_step. Converge mode: "master" or left out

magnitude.description: the probe's size as a fraction of the slider's per-pass maximum (default 0.5)

name: lr_set_regions
title: Set measured regions
description: Name parts of the photo (skin, fur, sky or custom) as boxes in 0-1 of the preview you see (the photo as cropped in Lightroom, upright), from its top-left corner, as mask geometry is; their metrics appear in every later `metrics.regions[]`, starting with the last preview (returned now). `preserve: true` guards a region: a pass that moves its mean hue more than 6 degrees or its mean saturation more than 8 points from now is undone. A mask pass's converged_by_metrics: every region's change is under the convergence thresholds (mean luma < 1/255, clipping < 0.1 point); false without regions or when the pass was undone; a signal only, the session goes on. The list replaces any earlier one. Does not touch Lightroom.

box.description: a box in 0-1 of the preview you see (the photo as cropped in Lightroom, upright), from its top-left corner: {x, y, w, h}

preserve.description: true: guard this region's hue and saturation from here on

regions.description: the whole set of regions (it replaces any earlier set); [] removes them

name: lr_select_variant
title: Pick a variant
description: Variants mode: continue the session on the copy the user picked (ask the user; do not pick for them). The copy is selected in Lightroom, later lr_step calls go to it, and its pass count carries on from its own passes. The other copies stay in the catalog as they are; the user removes them in Lightroom when they want. Returns the pick, its passes left and its last preview. Also accepted before every copy has had its refined pass. Does not render. If the user already picked in the HUD, calling this with that letter confirms it (`picked_by: "hud"`); another letter is refused.

name: lr_approve_pass
title: Approve the pass shown
description: approve_each_pass mode only: the user approves the pass they last saw, so the next lr_step may go ahead (the same as the HUD's Approve button). Call it ONLY after the user approved that pass in this chat, and set `confirmed: true` to state that they did; never call it on your own to get past AWAITING_APPROVAL. A waiting lr_step goes ahead at once. Returns `approved_pass`. Refused with NOT_AWAITING_APPROVAL in autonomous mode or when no pass waits for approval (pass 1 needs none; a Variants pick approves the pass it was picked at). Does not touch Lightroom.

confirmed.description: true only after the user approved the pass in this chat

name: lr_end_session
title: End the editing session
description: End the session. "accept": keep the edit; the log is finalised and a recipe (the final settings under canonical names) is written next to it. "revert": apply the pre-session snapshot, putting every setting back as it was before lr_begin_session (the result lists any setting that still differs). Returns the log and recipe paths and the final settings. Variants mode: "accept" needs a pick and keeps the pick's edit (the recipe is the pick's); "revert" puts the master back. Either way the copies stay in the catalog, listed in `copies`. After the user clicked Abort in the HUD, only "revert" is taken. Once the user ended the session on the Deck, the outcome matching theirs ("accept" after Accept; "revert" after Abort or Put back) returns ok with `already_ended_by_user` {outcome, source, at, log_path}; any other outcome gets SESSION_ENDED. "abandon": only when the session cannot end otherwise and the user agrees: Lightroom is gone or hung, or an AI mask failed or seems stuck (AI_MASK_FAILED, LIGHTROOM_STUCK, AI_UPDATE_PENDING refuse revert). It reads and writes nothing (it does not wait for Lightroom): the photo keeps what the session did and is NOT put back (`photo_put_back` false), the log's outcome is "abandoned", and a new session can begin. LIGHTROOM_STUCK and AI_UPDATE_PENDING lift once Lightroom's result shows, so try "revert" again first if the user can wait. The result's `note` says how the user puts the photo back by hand (the pre-session snapshot, `snapshot`) and whether Lightroom still holds writes to the photo (`lightroom_guard`: "none" when no AI mask was pending, so nothing is held; "cleared"; "not_cleared" or "plugin_too_old": held until Lightroom restarts; "kept": held until the mask's shape shows, so the user waits for it first); tell the user both. A session an engine that stopped left open (lr_get_active_photo_context `left_open`) is ended the same three ways, with `left_open: true` and the log's `ended_by` "recovery": revert applies its snapshot and says what it `checked`; accept reads the photo as it is now.

outcome.description: "accept" keeps the edit and writes the recipe; "revert" applies the pre-session snapshot; "abandon" ends a stuck session without touching the photo

name: lr_get_session_log
title: Session log
description: Return a session's provenance log (every pass: settings before/after, changes, metrics, preview hash, rationale, guardrail actions), open or ended. Does not touch Lightroom.

name: lr_list_masks
title: List the photo's masks
description: List the masks on the session's photo: id, name, kind (lr_create_mask's kinds; "ai", "range" or "other" for a kind Lightroom made that the tools do not know; "mixed" for components of several kinds), on/off, inverted, components, the local sliders not at 0 (Masking panel units), geometry, and for AI masks whether they have computed. Geometry, points and people's boxes are in 0-1 of the preview you see (the photo as cropped in Lightroom, upright), from its top-left corner, as lr_create_mask takes them; a mask drawn past the crop in Lightroom reads outside 0-1. On a mirrored photo geometry reads { unavailable: <why> }. A mask of several parts also lists `parts`, in order (lr_edit_mask `part` 1 is the first): each part's kind, mode (add, subtract, intersect; "other" for none of them), inverted and geometry. Also lists the local sliders and their ranges. Does not use a pass and writes nothing.

target.description: Variants mode: which photo ("master", "A", …); default the photo the last call worked on

name: lr_create_mask
title: Create a mask
description: Create one mask on the session's photo, with its local sliders set in the same pass. linear and radial take geometry; luminance takes geometry.lum_range; Lightroom finds and computes the AI kinds (the call waits up to 5 minutes; the Deck's Abort ends the wait: SESSION_ENDED). If the photo has none of that kind, MASK_NOTHING_FOUND: the mask is taken out again and the pass is not used. If Lightroom stays busy or shows a dialog, the HUD tells the user to click OK in it. If the mask then computes the pass goes on; if Lightroom reports the update failed or dropped it, the engine puts the photo back as it was before the session and ENDS the session (LIGHTROOM_DIALOG). No result in 5 minutes, or Lightroom not answering, is LIGHTROOM_STUCK: Lightroom's AI mask is still computing, nothing is written to the photo, and the session stays open and refuses writes, renders and reverts (AI_UPDATE_PENDING) until Lightroom's result shows. Lightroom does not notify you: when the user says to go on, your next call (lr_step, lr_end_session or a linear or radial mask; not the same AI mask again) picks it up. Tell the user to wait, or to press Abort in the Deck (lr_help, 9, says what it does). For the rest of the session prefer linear or radial masks to AI masks. If Lightroom reports the update over with no result, AI_MASK_FAILED: the user should save their work and restart Lightroom; start a new session only if they ask. If the update fails with a Lightroom or plugin error, subject, sky and background are made by Lightroom's Develop module instead (Lightroom then switches to Develop; `ai.route` "dc", `switched_to_develop`); people and landscape kinds have no such fallback. If nothing works, FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE (details.routes_tried): the masks are as before and the pass is not used. One person's kinds (person_*) take the person whose box holds the point: `ai.people` lists every person's box Lightroom found (left, top, right, bottom, in geometry's frame) and `ai.instance` the one chosen (lr_list_masks shows both); no person at the point: MASK_NOTHING_FOUND with the boxes. Each mask change is ONE pass of the session (it counts against max_passes, so raise max_passes at lr_begin_session when masks are planned; it may follow convergence, and approve_each_pass mode gates it like lr_step). A rename alone (lr_edit_mask with only mask_id and name) is not a pass: one History step, no render, and it works at the pass cap. A mask change writes the photo's whole mask table as one History step "AVG <id> pass n/N mask <op>", reads it back, renders and measures, and is undone ("… clip revert" / "… region revert"; the pass still counts) when clipping goes over a limit the photo was within, or a preserved region drifts; global sliders are never moved for a mask. To measure a local edit, name its area with lr_set_regions first: every mask pass returns its metrics in `metrics.regions[]` and `delta_metrics.regions[]`. converged_by_metrics: every region's change is under the convergence thresholds (mean luma < 1/255, clipping < 0.1 point); false without regions or when the pass was undone; a signal only, the session goes on. An AI mask's geometry.point is Lightroom's reference point (Lightroom may move it while it computes), not where the mask reaches. If the masks changed in Lightroom meanwhile: MASKS_CHANGED, nothing written. The other masks on the photo, the user's own included, are written back unchanged and checked on read-back. Editing a mask the tools cannot write back safely (several parts in a form not listed under lr_edit_mask, a blend mode on its first part, a kind not listed here) is refused: MASKS_UNCAPTURED_KIND, nothing written; deleting it is allowed. A mirrored photo refuses geometry and points (CROP_FRAME_UNSUPPORTED); `warnings` flags a mask 90 % or more outside the preview. Returns the mask, every mask of the photo (`masks`, with fresh ids), metrics, delta_metrics and the image. Needs plugin 0.16.0. color_range, depth_range, brush: not reshaped, not parts. Not offered: Select Objects, brush erase, mask pixels, mask presets.

target.description: Variants mode: masks go on the pick only (after lr_select_variant). Converge mode: "master" or left out

rationale.description: one line: what you saw and why this mask change

kind.description: linear, radial, luminance, depth_range, brush (geometry); color_range (point, color_amount). Found by Lightroom's AI: subject, sky, background; landscape, one category per mask: landscape_architecture, landscape_mountains, landscape_artificial_ground, landscape_natural_ground, landscape_vegetation, landscape_sky, landscape_water, landscape_snow; every person in the photo, one part per mask: people_face_skin, people_iris_pupil, people_body_skin, people_hair, people_lips, people_facial_hair, people_eye_sclera, people_eyebrows, people_clothes, people_teeth; one person, with point on them: person_entire, person_face_skin, person_iris_pupil, person_body_skin, person_hair, person_lips, person_facial_hair, person_eye_sclera, person_eyebrows, person_clothes, person_teeth. people, landscape (name the part or category) and objects are refused, with the reason

name.description: the name the Masks panel shows (default "AVG <kind>"); a suggested style is "N. Subject - Purpose", for example "4. Lone Juniper - Foliage Separation"; any clear name works

zero.description: linear: where the effect fades to nothing

full.description: linear: where the effect is full

lum_range.description: luminance: [a, b, c, d] in 0-1, each at least the one before: luminance a..d is masked, fully from b to c (at least 0.01 wide)

depth_range.description: depth_range: as lum_range, in distances, 0 the nearest; only on photos with a depth map (DEPTH_MAP_MISSING otherwise)

color_amount.description: color_range: how far the selection reaches from the colour at `point` (Lightroom's Refine), above 0 to 1, default 0.5

strokes.description: brush: 1-50 strokes painted with the mask's sliders (no erase)

points.description: the stroke's path; the engine fills in dabs between the points

radius.description: the brush's radius as a fraction of the whole photo's long edge (before any crop), default 0.05

geometry.description: In 0-1 of the preview you see (the photo as cropped in Lightroom, upright), from its top-left corner, as lr_get_preview `region` and lr_set_regions are; the engine maps it through the photo's crop (its angle included). linear: zero and full points; radial: the ellipse's box left, top, right, bottom (the ellipse is square to the preview); luminance: lum_range (tones, not a place); depth_range: depth_range; color_range: color_amount (the colour is `point`'s); brush: strokes. name: lr_edit_mask
title: Edit a mask
description: Change one mask by its id: set local sliders (absolute values in panel units; sliders not given keep their values), its geometry (linear, radial, luminance), invert it, rename it, or hide/show it (`active`). MASK_NOT_FOUND: call lr_list_masks for the current ids. Parts: `combine` adds a part (kind, geometry) in mode add, subtract or intersect; `part` names one part to reshape (geometry), invert, set to a mode (combine.mode) or remove (remove_part); a mask of several parts is inverted or reshaped only part by part. Only these forms, which were checked in Lightroom, are written: "linear, add radial", "linear, subtract radial", "linear, intersect radial", "radial, add sky", "radial, subtract sky", "radial, intersect sky", "sky, add radial", "linear, subtract linear", "radial, subtract radial", "radial, intersect luminance", "radial, subtract radial: reshape part 2", "radial, subtract radial: part 2 to intersect", "radial, subtract radial: remove part 2", "radial, intersect radial" (a mask's parts in order, each after the first with its mode; a part edit as "<form>: <edit>"; sky stands for every AI kind, though only sky was checked). name: lr_sync_series
title: Sync settings to other photos
description: Copy settings onto other photos: the recipe of a session that ended with accept ({session_id}), a recipe file ({recipe_path}), or canonical settings as absolute values ({settings}). Targets are the photos selected in Lightroom ("selected") or {uuids}; the photos are written by uuid and the selection is not changed. `parameter_mask` limits what is copied, by group. For each target the engine takes a Develop snapshot "AVG pre-sync <id>" (applying it undoes the sync), writes the copied settings as one History step "AVG sync <id>" and reads them back. adaptive_exposure (for bursts of the same scene): exposure is not copied; each target is rendered and its exposure moved ("AVG sync <id> exposure k", at most 4 renders of about 3.5 s) until its mean luma is within 2/255 of the source photo's; the source photo must still hold the recipe's settings (else SOURCE_CHANGED). At most 500 targets per call. A call works for about 30 seconds, then stops starting new photos and returns `not_yet` and `next`, saying how to go on: keep calling until `not_yet` is gone, and tell the user how far along it is. A call still busy at 50 seconds returns `pending` with `next`. Each call has its own sync id, so its photos' snapshots and History steps carry it. Tell the user which photos will change before calling. A target that fails is listed in `skipped` with the reason, and the others still sync; if Lightroom stops answering, the call stops and the error names the photo it stopped at and any step that may still have been written (`maybe_written`). Across pipelines (a raw recipe onto a JPEG, or the reverse) the shared groups are written and the target's `not_transferable` lists white_balance (Kelvin on raw, relative -100..100 on rendered: the numbers mean different things) and camera_profile (each pipeline has its own profiles) with the reason; a target that could take nothing is skipped (NOTHING_TRANSFERABLE). Returns applied, skipped, per_target_exposure_offsets (target exposure minus the source's), each target's pipeline, History steps, snapshot and not_transferable, and a contact sheet. Not while a session is open.
